record.original_question: Determine whether the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes, despite being false in full generality.

evidence.quote: It remains open if, as suggested by Klazar [33], the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris hold when restricted to finitely based permutation classes.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on growth rates of permutation classes (notably the "Growing at a Perfect Speed" line of research and follow-up papers by Bevan, Pantone, Vatter and others, ca. 2018–2020) shows that the analogous statements fail even within finitely based classes: the value ξ ≈ 2.30522 is an accumulation point from above of growth rates of finitely based permutation classes, and uncountable families/perfect sets of growth rates can be realized by finitely based classes. This refutes Klazar's suggestion and indicates the problem is solved in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Growth Rates of Permutation Classes: Categorization up to the Uncountability Threshold
status_evidence.snippet: Refutes a suggestion of Klazar; ξ ≈ 2.30522 is shown to be an accumulation point from above of growth rates of finitely based permutation classes.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás and Morris fail even for finitely based permutation classes.

status_evidence.title: Growing at a Perfect Speed
status_evidence.snippet: Exhibits permutation classes whose growth rates form a perfect set, refuting conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás and Morris.
status_evidence.claim: BBM conjectures on growth rates fail in general.
